title: Buried Services: Cables & Pipes
whatItIs: Hitting a buried electricity cable can cause an explosion and severe burns; gas from a damaged pipe can ignite. Find services before you dig, then dig with care.

keyFacts.text: Work that could disturb an underground service MUST NOT go ahead until steps are taken to prevent the risk.

keyFacts: Service plans are only a guide: they may be wrong or incomplete. Use a locator (CAT) as well.
Hand dig trial holes to find the exact position and depth. Plastic pipes can't be found by normal locators.
No hand-held power tools within 0.5 m of a cable's marked line; no excavator within 0.5 m of a gas pipe.
Treat every pipe or cable as live until known otherwise. A black plastic service? Assume a live cable.
If an excavator hits a cable, the driver should stay in the cab. Keep everyone else away.

visual.caption: Locate, then dig safely (HSG150 paras 371-379; HSG47)

items.title: Plans
items.text: Get plans from the utilities and landowner. Look for manholes, valve covers, street lights.

items.title: Locate and mark
items.text: A trained person traces services with a CAT; mark with paint or wooden pegs, not spikes.

items.title: Dig with care
items.text: Hand dig trial holes; dig alongside, not over, a service; recheck with the locator.

a.label: Hand-held power tools
points: Not within 0.5 m of a cable's marked line

b.label: Excavators
points: Not within 0.5 m of a gas pipe

onTheTest.question: You have the service plans for the area. What should happen before you dig?
options: Nothing: the plans show exact positions
Trace services with a locator and hand dig trial holes
Dig a test hole with the excavator
Probe the ground with a steel spike
onTheTest.why: HSG150 paras 372-375: plans are only a guide. Trained people use a locator (CAT), then trial holes are dug by hand to find the exact position and depth.

onTheTest.question: You uncover an unmarked black plastic service. How should you treat it?
options: As a telecoms cable that's safe to cut
onTheTest.why: HSG47 para 122: if any black plastic service is found, assume it is a live electricity cable. Treat all services as live until proved otherwise.

traps: Locators can miss things: plastic pipes, and cables carrying little or no current.
Two trial holes don't prove a service runs in a straight line between them.
Cables can be shallow: most injuries involve 415-volt cables within 0.5 m of the surface.
Use spades and shovels, not picks or forks, which are more likely to pierce cables.
